newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts hold gains on heat.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts hold gains on heat.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Tuesday in a fairly active session, with front months lifted by reports of further gains in the cash from hot weather over much of the nation, sources said.
July gained four cents to close at $2.286 per million British thermal units. August settled 2.7 cents higher at $2.269. Other deferreds ended mixed.

"We broke through $2.28 (basis July), which was a big number. It was a very constructive close and it should take us into the low-$2.30s or higher," said one East Coast trader, noting July finished near the day's high.

With some unplanned nuclear plant outages expected to last through the week and mostly above-normal U.S. temperatures forecast into early next week, some players anticipated a fairly strong bidweek later in the week.
But they said the bears should quickly emerge when temperatures moderate.
In the East, unplanned outages were reported at PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1, GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 and Duke's 846 MW Oconee 3, and all were expected to remain off line for most of the week.
Early estimates for a build in Wednesday's weekly AGA gas storage report range from 70 bcf to 95 bcf.

Technical traders said July's close Tuesday above resistance in the $2.27-2.28 area should lead to a test of the $2.36-2.37 area. Further resistance was seen at the contract high of $2.44. Support remained at the $2.151 double bottom, then at $2.13, $2.055 and $2.

In the cash Tuesday, Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly to near the $2.30 level. Midcon pipes gained a similar amount to the low-teens. New York city gate gas was quoted about five cents higher in the low-$2.60s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 1.3 cents to $2.302. NYMEX said 54,900 contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 36,430.
NYMEX July natgas futures expire Thursday, June 26.

On the KCBT, July finished 2.9 cents higher at $2.149, while deferreds ended up by one to two cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.1 cents to 13.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 542 lots traded, down slightly from Monday's total of 552.
KCBT July natgas futures expire Wednesday, June 25.
